Vulnérabilité critique CVE-2026-89324 (score CVSS 9.8).

The Basel Post Types plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Authentication Bypass in all versions up to, and including, 1.18. The vulnerability exists because a missing-quotes coding error in the defined() call for SECURE_AUTH_SALT inside BASEL_Auth::get_config() causes PHP to evaluate the constant's value rather than its name, making the check always fail and permanently falling back to the static hardcoded salt 2NlBUibcszrVtNmDnxqDbwCOpLWq91eatIz6O1O that is publicly visible in the theme source code; because this salt is static and known, an attacker can compute a valid Opauth signature entirely offline and submit a forged ?opauth callback to the unauthenticated init hook endpoint processed by register_or_login. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to authenticate as any existing WordPress user, including administrators, by forging a callback tied to a known target account email address — bypassing all password verification, multi-factor authentication, and ownership checks, and receiving a fully authenticated session cookie via wc_set_customer_auth_cookie(). Exploitation requires WooCommerce to be active and at least one Basel social-login provider (Facebook, Google, or VKontakte) to be configured with a valid app_id and app_secret in the theme settings.

Score CVSS : 9.8

Type de faiblesse (CWE) : CWE-287

items.detail:
Incident de sécurité rapporté par CyberScoop.

A ransomware attack discovered Monday at Vanderbilt University in Nashville, Tennessee appears to have compromised vast amounts of student and employee personal data, prompting the university to take several digital services intermittently offline as it continues responding to the incident. As of Tuesday morning, the university shared an update that select campus-wide systems and applications were safe to use again, including campus WiFi, Okta, Outlook, Brightspace, Zoom and YES, while others remain restricted, including CampusPrint. Students, faculty and staff were also allowed to resume use of Vanderbilt devices, following orders to shut them down Monday.  “Vanderbilt Information Technology continues to work with government agencies and other partners to manage this situation, and we will continue to send updates today and throughout this week for as long as necessary,” the update said.  A ransomware group known as BYOD has taken responsibility for the attack, according to a post on the group’s leak blog. Fireworks said the incident affected a “limited number of customer accounts” — all of whom were notified of the attack.

AI infrastructure company Fireworks said cybercriminals stole billing information and AI-specific data during two breaches last month.

Fireworks published an updated notice on Monday saying it hired Palo Alto Networks Unit 42 to investigate a data breach it initially discovered on October 6 . The San Mateo-based company was founded in 2022 and has more than 10,000 customers, offering an array of AI systems and tools to companies.

Investigators found that a well-known, financially motivated cybercriminal group launched the attack and stole account and billing information as well as secrets — confidential digital pieces of information that grant access to human users or apps and allow them to communicate or perform actions. Fireworks said the incident affected a “limited number of customer accounts” — all of whom were notified of the attack.

Monday’s alert from Fireworks also notes that the company experienced another incident on October 23 where a third-party cloud provider that hosted their R&D machines was attacked by cybercriminals.

“On October 24, the unauthorized third party used [the provider] to reach Fireworks development machines and then run an unauthorized workload that led to additional customer data impact,” the company said.

The hackers gained access to internal Fireworks data, billing information, invoices and payment history as well as datasets and other AI-related data.

A 41-year-old U.S. Army soldier was arrested on suspicion of spying for Russia, British authorities announced Tuesday.

The unnamed soldier was arrested by U.K. counterterrorism police “working closely” with U.S. authorities, including the FBI and the military, the Metropolitan Police said in a statement. The man is in custody at a London police station.

“While this investigation is continuing, I want to send a clear message—this FBI has no tolerance for anyone who breaks their oath to the United States and whose actions endanger our national security and that of our partners,” FBI Director Kash Patel said in a statement issued by the British counter-terror police.

The man was arrested under sections of the U.K.’s National Security Act that cover espionage. The arrest occurred near Gloucester, a city about 100 miles west of London that is close to the home of GCHQ, Britain’s intelligence, security and cybersecurity agency.

“As part of the investigation officers are carrying out searches at two locations in Gloucestershire,” according to police. “The country to which the allegations relate is Russia.”

Brig. Gen. Sean Stinchon, the head U.S. Army Counterintelligence Command, said in a statement that the “senior soldier” who was arrested was “entrusted with sensitive information.”

Signal de veille — The Record.

Michael LoSapio, Palantir's chief information security officer, is officially President Donald Trump's pick to lead the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency.

President Donald Trump has nominated the chief information security officer of Palantir to lead the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency, potentially marking a turning point for an organization that has endured massive staff cuts and years of Republican attacks.

The president selected Michael LoSapio on Monday as the next head of the top civilian cyber defense agency, which has been without a Senate-confirmed leader since Trump returned to the Oval Office. A previous nominee, Sean Plankey, withdrew from consideration earlier this year after spending months in limbo on Capitol Hill; Nick Andersen has led CISA in an acting capacity since February.

The Homeland Security Department’s cyber wing lost more than 1,000 personnel — one-third of its workforce — and has seen its budget slashed by billions during the second Trump administration, following years of GOP complaints that its efforts to combat online disinformation during elections singled out conservative voices and infringed upon free speech rights.

As a result, CISA remained largely behind the scenes ahead of last week’s midterm elections. However, a spokesperson said the organization “provided voluntary, no-cost services” like vulnerability scanning ahead of Election Day and activated its Incident Coordination Group to serve as a threat information sharing hub.

items.detail:
Signal de veille — The Register.

President Donald Trump has nominated Palantir security chief Michael LoSapio to lead CISA, putting an executive from the controversial government supplier in line to run America's civilian cyber defense agency. The nomination, announced on Monday, could end CISA's nearly two-year wait for a Senate-confirmed director following Jen Easterly's departure in January 2025. LoSapio has served as Palantir's CISO since September 2024, having previously led the company's infrastructure and network security team. He first joined the data analytics outfit in 2013, later spent a spell at database company SingleStore, and returned to Palantir in 2017. If confirmed, LoSapio would move from securing Palantir's systems to leading the federal government's main civilian cyber defense agency. CISA protects federal civilian networks and works with critical infrastructure operators, including power, water, and telecommunications providers. It's a substantial job, particularly given the state of the agency he would inherit. CISA has shed more than 1,000 staff, roughly a third of its workforce, since Trump returned to the White House, according to reports. The house of Bezos announced the launch of Ring Robotics on Tuesday along with its first two products: a drone designed for indoor home security, and a wheeled robot with a telescoping camera mast for automated after-hours business patrols. Both are designed to proactively patrol spaces as well as respond to alerts from connected alarm systems and Ring-connected devices. According to Ring founder Jamie Siminoff, this is something customers actually want, as those stationary cameras just can’t quite see everywhere. “It’s not just a new category of security; it’s the beginning of a future where proactive, autonomous protection is something every home and every business can have,” Siminoff said.
